title: Humphrey's lessons and his club orchestra
summary: Details of the lessons: twice a week, 50 cents, at Humphrey's home, and the club orchestra rehearsing at members' houses.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well, we played about two years. Well, I was going to ask some more about your lessons with Jim Humphrey. Well. How often did you go? Oh, I used to go twice a week.
Where did they teach? At his home, or where did he live up from?
At his home. He lived on, in the 4500 block on Liberty Street.
Way uptown. Mm-hmm. How much did you charge for a lesson, do you remember? 50 cents. 50? Those are private lessons or... Private. Not a class? No, private lessons.
He had an orchestra. And the orchestra had... Used to go around to different ones' houses and they'd practice each week.
Every day they had a certain night. They'd go and the club used to furnish the refreshments.
Well, they didn't have nothing but cake and ice cream and salt drinks, something like that.
Yeah. Like a party would make out.

Yeah. And each week, the different students would meet. Those would, well, you know, were advanced enough to play in the officers. Yeah. And then they would probably play at maybe some church benefit or something like that. All right. They had a house party. And some of the club members' houses and different things all the time.
